title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
description: Discover free social and recreational activities across Berry College's expansive 27,000-acre campus, from historic landmarks to scenic nature trails.

cards.title: Cycle the Viking Trail
cards.subtitle: A 3-mile paved path for students and visitors
cards.notes: Ride or walk this paved 3-mile trail connecting the main campus to the mountain campus. It is open daily during daylight hours for cyclists and joggers.
cards.short_summary: The Viking Trail is a 3-mile paved path connecting Berry's main and mountain campuses for free recreational use.
cards.evidence_claim: The Viking Trail is a three-mile paved trail for walkers, runners, cyclists and rollerbladers, open during daylight hours.
cards.source_title: Campus Use and Recreation - Berry College
cards.access_notes: Open daily during daylight hours; accessible from the Ladd Center.

cards.title: Hike to the House o' Dreams
cards.subtitle: Historic retreat atop Lavender Mountain
cards.notes: Trek the 2.4-mile trail up Lavender Mountain to reach this historic stone cottage. The grounds offer panoramic views and are open to the public for free.
cards.short_summary: The House o' Dreams is a historic stone retreat on Lavender Mountain accessible via a free public hiking trail.
cards.evidence_claim: The trail up the mountain to the house is open to the public and there is no fee to tour the house or the tower.
cards.source_title: Trail Destinations and Heads - Berry College
cards.access_notes: Accessible via the main entrance; visitors must check in at the Welcome Center for a map.

cards.title: Visit the Martha Berry Museum
cards.subtitle: Free admission for the Berry community
cards.notes: Explore exhibits on the college's history and founder Martha Berry. Self-guided tours of the museum building are free for all guests.
cards.short_summary: The Martha Berry Museum offers free self-guided tours detailing the history of the college and its founder.
cards.evidence_claim: A self-guided tour of The Martha Berry Museum is free to all guests.
cards.source_title: Berry College Oak Hill Museum Tours
cards.access_notes: Open Monday through Saturday, 10 a.m. to 5 p.m.

cards.title: Relax by the Ford Reflection Pool
cards.subtitle: Gothic architecture and scenic waters
cards.notes: Visit the iconic Ford Complex to see the English Gothic-style buildings and the large reflection pool, a popular spot for photography and quiet study.
cards.short_summary: The Ford Reflection Pool is a scenic landmark within the Gothic-style Ford Complex, open for public viewing and photography.
cards.evidence_claim: Mirror pools surrounding the building provide beautiful photo backdrops; the site is open for public campus use.
cards.source_title: Ford Buildings at Berry College - Georgia's Rome
cards.access_notes: Visitors must enter through the main gate and present ID at the Welcome Center.

cards.title: Watch the Swans at Swan Lake
cards.subtitle: A peaceful campus wildlife habitat
cards.notes: Walk around Swan Lake to spot the resident trumpeter swans. It is a quiet, scenic area perfect for nature observation and birdwatching.
cards.short_summary: Swan Lake is a campus habitat home to resident swans, offering a free and peaceful nature experience.
cards.evidence_claim: Swan Lake and Berry College are home to swans once again; the area is part of the campus open for public use.
cards.source_title: Swans on the Lake - Berry College
cards.access_notes: Open during daylight hours as part of the main campus grounds.

cards.title: Play the Log Cabin Disc Golf Course
cards.subtitle: 18-hole course on the main campus
cards.notes: Challenge friends to a round on this 18-hole course. Students can check out discs for free from the Cage Center equipment desk.
cards.short_summary: The Log Cabin Disc Golf Course is a free 18-hole facility on campus with equipment available for student checkout.
cards.evidence_claim: Berry College students and faculty/staff can check out discs from the Cage Center; the course is free to play.
cards.access_notes: The first tee is located near the campus chapel; guests must enter through the Visitor's Center.

cards.title: Tee Off at WinShape Course
cards.subtitle: Secondary course near WinShape Centre
cards.notes: Explore the second on-campus disc golf course located behind the WinShape tennis courts. It offers a different terrain for experienced players.
cards.short_summary: The WinShape Disc Golf Course provides a second free 18-hole layout for students and visitors on the mountain campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The WinShape Course 1st Tee is located behind the WinShape Centre Tennis Courts.
cards.access_notes: Located on the mountain campus; open during daylight hours.

cards.title: Spot Deer and Wildlife
cards.subtitle: Nature observation on 27,000 acres
cards.notes: Drive or walk through campus to see the famous deer population. The campus serves as a wildlife refuge with thousands of deer roaming freely.
cards.short_summary: Berry College's vast campus is a wildlife refuge where visitors can observe deer and other animals for free.
cards.evidence_claim: Berry is known for its large numbers of deer; over 15,000 acres fall under the care of the Georgia DNR as a wildlife refuge.
cards.source_title: Campus Use and Recreation - Berry College
cards.access_notes: Best viewed at dawn or dusk; visitors must stay on designated roads and trails.

cards.title: Stroll the Campus Arboretum
cards.subtitle: Educational tree walk on main campus
cards.notes: Follow the self-guided tree walk to learn about the diverse species in the Berry College Arboretum. It is an educational and free outdoor activity.
cards.short_summary: The Berry College Arboretum features a free self-guided tree walk showcasing the campus's diverse botanical collection.
cards.evidence_claim: Berry College established specific trail designations including the Arboretum and Tree Walk.
cards.source_title: Trail Destinations and Heads - Berry College
cards.access_notes: Located on the main campus; maps are available online or at the Welcome Center.

cards.title: Hike the Victory Lake Loop
cards.subtitle: Scenic lakeside trail for students
cards.notes: Walk the loop around Victory Lake for views of the water and surrounding forest. It is a popular spot for student hammocking and relaxation.
cards.short_summary: The Victory Lake Loop is a free hiking trail offering scenic lakeside views and recreational space for students.
cards.evidence_claim: The Department of Recreation manages trails around Victory Lake; it is a popular spot for hiking and relaxing in a hammock.
cards.access_notes: Accessible via the mountain campus; open during daylight hours.
